item.title: How a young woman became an ISIS bride — and then an informant, helping save others
item.description: A young Canadian mother shares her memories of being an ISIS bride, and her harrowing escape from the extremist group.

item.title: REMEMBERING LOVED ONES KILLED IN UNITED 93 CRASH
item.description: On September 11, 2001 Lori Guadagno lost her brother on flight United 93. 25 years later, the crash site is a place where she feels a sense of connection that she can't find anywhere else.
item.content:encoded: On September 11, 2001 Lori Guadagno lost her brother on flight United 93. 25 years later, the crash site is a place where she feels a sense of connection that she can't find anywhere else.

item.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court deports legal US resident to Afghanistan in first-ever case
item.description: Nazira Haji Zada, a lawful permanent resident, conceded to being an "alien terrorist." It marks the first case in the Alien Terrorist Removal Court.

item.title: Manhattan's Trinity Church unveils new pipe organ, replacing one damaged in 9/11 attacks
item.description: Manhattan's Trinity Church marked the 25th anniversary of 9/11 with a concert featuring a new cathedral-sized pipe organ, replacing the hundred-year-old instrument damaged in the attacks.

item.title: Miami crash raises concerns about the jet's operator, and why it's flying for Amazon
item.description: The cargo plane crash in Miami is raising concerns about the safety culture at 21 Air, one of the carriers that fly for Amazon. Former pilots were sounding alarms even before Sunday's accident.

item.description: The assassination of far right activist Charlie Kirk opened the floodgates of neighbor-on-neighbor doxing. A year later, the damage to political discourse in the U.S. remains.

item.title: As diseases loom, CDC's response to measles deaths stirs fears about agency's reliability
item.description: The worst U.S. measles outbreak in decades is growing and flu season is imminent. Experts are fretting about federal health data reliability after the CDC questioned two Pennsylvania measles deaths.
